To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

STN8, a kinase that is responsible for the phosphorylation of the photosystem II core proteins, is also responsible for the phosphorylations of the photosystem inner antenna subunit, CP29, and that the antagonist of STN8, PBCP, dephosphorylates CP29 in high light.
STN8 kinase and its antagonist PBCP phosphatases are responsible for reversible phosphorylation of rice PSII inner antenna CP29.
the STN8 kinase-PBCP phosphatases system is responsible for the high-light induced reversible phosphorylation of PSII inner antenna CP29 in rice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the enzymes that control reversible phosphorylation of PSII antenna proteins in HL.
the identification of the enzymes involved in the reversible phosphorylation of thlalkoid proteins in rice, which is the most relevant crop in the world.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the HL-dependent reversible thylakoid phosphorylation in rice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the STN8‐PBCP system is responsible for the reversible phosphorylation of PSII proteins in rice.

the OsSTN7 kinase, the OsSTN6 kinase, the OsPBCP and the OsSTN1 phosphatases are responsible for the reversible phosphorylation of LHCII and the PSII core proteins, whereas the OsSTN2, OsSTN8 and OsPBCP enzymes are responsible for the HL-induced reversible phosphorylation of CP29.
in monocots, the HL response involves two distinct sets of kinases and phosphatases that act on different targets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
STN8 and STN7 kinases are the key players for the reversible phosphorylation of PSII in monocots.
the STN8-PBCP system is responsible for both the repair of photo-inactivated PSII and the reversible phosphorylation of CP29 in HL.

the phosphorylation of PSII proteins in rice is catalyzed by a kinase-phosphatase pair, as in Arabidopsis, with the exception of the CP29 inner antenna, whose phosphorylation is catalyzed in rice by the STN8 kinase, but not by its antagonistic phosphatase PBCP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the STN8-PBCP system is involved in the regulation of the PSII-LHCII complex under HL, in addition to its role in the repair of damaged PSII.

the same set of enzymes that are responsible for the repair of photo-inactivated photosystem II (i.e., the STN8 kinase and its antagonist PBCP) are also responsible for reversible phosphorylation of photosystem II (photosystem I) under high-light conditions.
, in addition to the STN7-PPH1 system, the STN8-PBCP system is also involved in light-induced reversible phosphorylation of LHCII.
